verified.exploit_entry_point: AppService event dispatch through the project's own test harness: type:m.room.message events reach MatrixHandler.onMessage -> sendIrcAction, and type:m.room.member events reach the join handler; referenced reply/edit targets are resolved with the bridge bot's client and the result is written to the mock IRC client. Hidden tests drive the real dispatch and assert on the IRC line.
sites: src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:388 (member events observed; no arrival tracking at pinned)
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1050-1080 (edit original resolved and diffed with no visibility check)
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1284-1304 (reply target fetched with the bot intent; fetched room/time trusted; cache written under the response ids)
src/bridge/MatrixHandler.ts:1323,1359 (referenced text formatted into the long reply and sent)
src/util/MessageDiff.ts:38,68 (removed words of the fetched original become the IRC text)
routes: T1 reply guard: a cached or fetched reply target is quoted for a sender who arrived after it was relayed, or whose arrival time the homeserver fabricates
T2 fetched target time: a fetched target carrying a far-future homeserver timestamp defeats a join-time comparison
T3 fetched target identity: a fetched response naming another room, or no room at all, is still quoted and cached
T4 edit: the edit branch diffs against the original and emits its removed words, with no visibility check; the bridge library's sender check is passed when a lying homeserver answers for the editor
verified.project_tests_run: spec/integ/matrix-to-irc.spec.js (the revision shipped with the first published fix), spec/unit/MessageDiff.spec.js, spec/unit/TrimString.spec.js: 41 tests pass at the pinned commit and under the reference fix, and are part of the graded functional group.
verified.not_routes_at_pinned: Admin-room authorization (reader T4) and the media-preview length arithmetic (reader T5) are outside these advisories' content-disclosure protection and are not built. The sender-membership route (reader T3) has no fair behavioural test through the appservice entry point (the protocol already asserts the sender), so it is substituted by the published follow-up's timestamp-evidence lever.

traps.shape: the published fixes' route: a referenced message is quoted only when the referring sender was present before the bridge relayed it; the arrival evidence must be what the bridge saw, not the homeserver's timestamp; covers cached and fetched references
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The reported example is one reference resolved with the bridge's own access; a same-room lookup looks sufficient, the only timestamp attached to an arrival is the homeserver's own, and the bridge library already rejects edits whose parent sender differs.
security_tests: security::referenced message content withholds a cached source the replier joined after
security::referenced message content withholds a fetched source the replier joined after
security::referenced message content withholds a source when the arrival time is fabricated
security::referenced message content withholds a cached source dated after the replier joined
coupled_functional_tests: functional::legitimate relay behaviour keeps a quoted source for a member already present
functional::legitimate relay behaviour keeps a quoted source when the member joined before the message
traps.realistic_because: both published advisories live on this route: the reply guard (GHSA-wm4w-7h2q-3pf7) and the homeserver-timestamp reliance of that guard (GHSA-w9mh-5x8j-9754)

traps.shape: the time attached to a fetched target is homeserver-supplied; a far-future value makes a late-joining sender look present, and the value must be bounded by the bridge's own clock
traps.reason_to_dismiss: origin_server_ts is the only timestamp available for a fetched event, and the homeserver is its authority; the sample config already notes that clocks differ between homeservers.
security_tests: security::referenced message content withholds a fetched source dated after the replier joined
coupled_functional_tests: functional::legitimate relay behaviour keeps a quoted source for a fetched message in the same room
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code still present on the project's current development branch

traps.shape: a fetched response is used without checking that it names the room that was asked about; an absent room id must not pass either
traps.reason_to_dismiss: getEvent is called with the incoming room id and the cache is room-keyed, so the homeserver is assumed to enforce same-room access and its response identity is treated as authoritative.
security_tests: security::referenced message content withholds a fetched source that belongs to another room
security::referenced message content withholds a fetched source whose room is not stated
coupled_functional_tests: functional::legitimate relay behaviour keeps a quoted source for a fetched message in the same room
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code; the published fixes never compare the response's room with the requested room

traps.shape: the edit branch diffs the sender-supplied new text against the referenced original and emits the removed words with no visibility check; the bridge library's sender check trusts the homeserver's answer about the parent
traps.reason_to_dismiss: The FIXME presents the fetch as a known accepted limitation, only a short s/old/new/ diff is emitted rather than the whole original, and the bridge library already rejects an edit whose parent's sender differs.
security_tests: security::referenced message content withholds original words from an edit the editor joined after
coupled_functional_tests: functional::legitimate relay behaviour keeps the diff for an edit by the message author
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: neither published fix touches the edit branch

patch_checks.why: fresh agent (deepseek-flash[1m]), full view (instruction, tree, tests, reference, trap list)

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the protected operation builds outbound IRC text; there is no read/write or verb pair on this surface
wrong_fix_catalogue.malformed_identity: n/a: the decision compares opaque identifiers and numeric times; it parses no spelling that could be malformed
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: an arrival the bridge never saw is deliberately treated as present since the bridge started, which is the existing legitimate behaviour; there is no secret or role lookup that can fail open
wrong_fix_catalogue.adjacent_api: n/a: the reference fix adds a local decision inside one handler and changes no shared helper's stated behaviour

A.summary: Matrix IRC bridge truncated content of messages can be leaked through a reply

B.summary: The reply fix relied on homeserver-supplied origin_server_ts, which a malicious homeserver can fabricate
